result_semantic_payload.summary: The device holds a small but coherent evidentiary footprint of a crypto-denominated payment-collection operation. Two in-scope items carry the substance: (1) /data/收款记录.txt, a three-row collection ledger recording dated USDT receipts from three distinct payers (陈某 30,000 USDT to bank card 6222020212345678901 on 2023-11-02; 周某 17,500 USDT and 吴某 52,000 USDT both to wallet 0xDEAD1111 on 2023-11-04 and 2023-11-09 — total 99,500 USDT), which evidences both the collection activity and the off-ramp channels (one fiat bank card, one reused crypto wallet); and (2) /platform/说明.txt, internal platform notes naming the platform '聚宝盆', its admin console at http://jbpenl-admin.example, and a per-customer-service-group daily new-user recruitment quota of 20 — this ties the ledger to an organized platform operation with recruitment pressure rather than isolated transactions. The README.txt at the root is a scope note, not substantive proof, but it independently corroborates the intended evidentiary partition. The one document that must stay out of the evidentiary chain is /personal/体检报告.txt, a 2023-10-20 medical checkup report for 陈某: it is the owner's private health record, it explicitly states it is unrelated to any financial activity, and citing it as evidence of the payment operation would be improper (and the shared surname 陈某 with the first ledger payer is a coincidence, not a linkage). Scope caveat: this is a file-level extraction of 4 text files, not a Windows forensic image — there are no registry, prefetch, amcache, event-log or account-logon artifacts, so no execution or account-usage corroboration is available, and all four files share a single synthetic mtime/ctime.

claim_candidates.text: /data/收款记录.txt is a payment-collection ledger recording three dated USDT receipts totalling 99,500 USDT from three named payers (陈某 30,000 on 2023-11-02; 周某 17,500 on 2023-11-04; 吴某 52,000 on 2023-11-09), and it is the primary in-scope evidence of the payment-collection operation.
The ledger names two off-ramp channels: one fiat bank card (6222020212345678901) for the 陈某 payment and one crypto wallet (0xDEAD1111) reused for both the 周某 and 吴某 payments.

/platform/说明.txt identifies an internal platform '聚宝盆', an admin console URL (http://jbpenl-admin.example) and a per-customer-service-group daily new-user recruitment quota of 20, situating the ledger within an organized recruitment-driven platform operation.

The combination of a USDT collection ledger with a platform recruitment quota is consistent with an organized payment-collection operation rather than isolated one-off transfers, but the available artifacts do not establish the platform's business purpose or legality.
limitations: No chat, transaction-confirming or platform-side artifacts are present; the linkage between the ledger and the platform is by co-location and consistency only, not by a shared identifier.

claim_candidates.text: /personal/体检报告.txt (a 2023-10-20 medical checkup report for 陈某) must be excluded from the evidentiary chain: it is private health information, it states it is unrelated to any financial activity, and the shared surname 陈某 with the first ledger payer is not a linkage.

README.txt at the root is an in-scope scope note that partitions the collection: /data holds payment records, /platform holds platform operation notes, and /personal holds private documents with no evidential relation to the payment operation that must not be cited as evidence of it.

limitations: Task metadata reports no platform scenario and no registered source scopes, so the requested 'windows' scope resolved to a 4-file text extraction rather than a Windows forensic image.

No registry, prefetch, amcache, browser, account or event-log artifacts are present; therefore no execution, account-usage or authorship corroboration is possible, and the L2 execution-corroboration rule could not be applied.
All four files share identical mtime/ctime (1790594136), so file timestamps carry no investigative value.
No md5 values are recorded for any file, so integrity verification of the cited files cannot be established from this evidence set.
The linkage between the collection ledger and the platform notes rests on co-location and internal consistency only; no shared identifier connects them.
The platform name, admin URL, payer names and wallet/card identifiers are taken verbatim from unverified text files and have not been independently confirmed.
warnings: The medical checkup report contains private health information about a named individual and must not be cited as evidence of the payment operation; it should be retained under lawful basis only and kept segregated from the evidentiary chain.
Do not treat the shared surname 陈某 between the first ledger payer and the medical report subject as a link between the two documents.
